body:
WHAT IS REALLY THERE TODAY (code read 6 Nov 2026, main 068c71a; not run). The task text stays the definition.

APP
 * Prepare callers: only the Top search result (features/search/search_results.dart:57) and the first song of an opened catalogue album (features/instant/instant_warmup.dart:15,24), both through `InstantController.prepare` -> `EncoreInstantBackend.prepare` (data/encore/encore_instant.dart:120), which only resolves a row, as the task's re-read says. Nothing prepares the first 3 songs of an opened playlist or imported playlist.
 * The player's own preload is ONE song: the window is the current song plus the next (`_loadCurrentBody` 1061-1105, `_syncWindowTail` 1173-1206). The class comment (playback_engine.dart:55) says "at most three sources"; the code holds two. So "the next 2 songs of the queue" is NOT covered by the window: only the next one is. Correct the comment, and decide whether the second one is wanted (it costs one more paced YouTube slot per song).
 * Small defect, read not run: `_syncWindowTail` does not catch a failed resolve of the next song (`_loadCurrentBody` does, 1065-1069). In `_onBackendIndex` (1252-1289) a server blip during a gapless advance throws before `_emitAll()` and the immediate persist; the window keeps one source until the song ends (`_onCompleted` then recovers). Use the same `onError: null` pattern; test: a resolver that throws for the next song (`FakeResolver`, playback_engine_test.dart:19).

SERVER
 * The scheduler defines a `prepare` kind (priority 1, interactive pool: scheduler.py:31-34, docs/04 section 10) with no producer and no handler: `create_app` registers only `handlers["keep"]` (api.py:1361). There is no `POST refs/prepare` route, and docs/17 section 3 does not list it as planned: add it to the planned column in the PR that builds it. The task's "Context: `POST /api/prepare` exists (resolve + park 20 min)" describes the legacy fetch service (server/legacy/encore-fetch), not the Encore server.
 * The pacer is shared: every YouTube operation passes one pacer (mean 12 s, `sources/youtube/pace.py`, `source.py:108-112`; B-42(b)), and keeps share it. A prepare must not queue behind 200 background keeps: give it its own priority at the pacer, or the 1 s promise is false whenever somebody imports a playlist (B-39 is the same family).

MEASURE (standing rule: at most 10 YouTube look-ups per run, spaced): `tools/journeys/play_timing.py` on the test VM; the task's N2 number must exist before the server route is built, because it spends the owner's YouTube budget.
